subject: Geopolitics
title: Deep-Sea Mining Frontier
description: A micro-lesson that makes Deep-Sea Mining Frontier usable.

hook.text: Trillions of dollars in minerals sit on the ocean floor. No one has mined them yet. The race to start is heating up.

buildup.text: Polymetallic nodules contain nickel, cobalt, manganese, and copper — all essential for batteries and electronics.

discovery.text: The International Seabed Authority governs deep-sea mining. But rules aren't finished and pressure to start is intense.

twist.text: Environmentalists warn that mining the seabed could devastate deep-ocean ecosystems we barely understand.

climax.text: China, South Korea, and Norway lead the push. The ocean floor may become the next geopolitical battleground.

punchline.text: The next gold rush happens four miles underwater.

quiz.question: What are polymetallic nodules?
options: Artificial structures placed to monitor ocean currents
Deep-sea mineral deposits containing nickel, cobalt, and copper
Underwater volcanic formations near tectonic plates
